prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Cloudflare Workers on the free plan (requests per day, CPU time per request). Cite Cloudflare's own documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on my research into Cloudflare's official documentation, here are the documented limits for the Workers free plan.

The primary resource limits for the free plan are defined by a daily request quota and a maximum CPU time per individual request.

**Request Limit (per day):**
The free plan allows for 100,000 requests per day, measured across all of a user's Workers.
SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#worker-plan-limits | QUOTE: "Free: 100,000 requests per day" | CLAIM: The free plan has a limit of 100,000 requests per day.

**CPU Time (per request):**
The free plan allows a maximum of 10 milliseconds of CPU time per request. It's important to note that this limit is for the time the CPU is actively processing, not the total duration of the request (which can be longer if waiting for network calls).
SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#cpu-time | QUOTE: "Free: 10ms" | CLAIM: The free plan has a CPU time limit of 10 milliseconds per request.

**Additional Notes:**
This CPU time limit is strictly enforced. If a request on the free plan exceeds 10ms of CPU time, it will be terminated and will return an error.
SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#cpu-time | QUOTE: "If your request exceeds the CPU time limit for your plan, it will be terminated." | CLAIM: Exceeding the CPU time limit results in the request being terminated.

These are the two core, officially documented limits for the free plan that you asked about. Other general limits (like script size, subrequests, etc.) apply to all plans but are not specific to the free tier.
